What the DBMS guarantees: A confirmed change is on durable storage and survives a closed program or a power failure
Declared constraints are checked at every insertion and change; a row that breaks one is refused
Many users work at the same time; no change is lost and no half-finished change is read
Each user is identified and may carry out only the operations that have been granted
The database can be copied, and restored to a correct state after a failure
The user states which data are wanted and the DBMS works out how to retrieve them (SQL, ISO/IEC 9075)
